title: Large Bricks and Join-irreducible torsionfree classes

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof does not establish that every proper quotient of F is torsion. It claims that this can be reduced to checking 'every maximal quotient of F,' but then considers a nonzero map S -> F from a simple module and proves that coker(S -> F) is torsion. Such a cokernel is a quotient by a simple submodule, not a maximal/simple quotient of F. Moreover, an arbitrary quotient of the generally infinite-dimensional direct limit F need not have a maximal submodule or a simple quotient, so checking simple quotients would not imply that all proper quotients are torsion. This invalidates the asserted lim f-simple conclusion.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Proposition 3.9, construction after choosing a spanning tree T
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: A spanning tree of the underlying undirected Hasse graph does not in general define a directed system (a filtered diagram). The proof calls the oriented tree T' a 'directed acyclic subquiver' and then applies Lemma 3.6 to its colimit, but acyclicity of the arrow orientation is not the directedness condition required of an indexing category: any two vertices must have a common upper index. Removing Hasse edges to form a spanning tree can destroy common upper bounds. The statement that 'we don't have any compatibility condition to check ... as the underlying graph is a tree' only addresses path commutativity; it does not make the indexing diagram filtered. Thus the object constructed is not shown to satisfy the hypotheses of Lemma 3.6.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proposition 3.9, conclusion that B is a brick
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proposition asserts existence of a 'brick B,' but the proof only obtains a torsionfree, almost torsion module B from Lemma 3.7. It never proves End_Lambda(B) is a division ring. Proposition 3.5 identifies such a B with a simple object of the HRS heart, from which brickness could be deduced only after additionally stating and using that Hom in the heart between the relevant torsionfree modules agrees with Hom_Lambda. That necessary argument is absent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and introductory statement of the main aim versus the standing notation and Proposition 3.9
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract claims the result for 'finitely generated modules over an artinian ring.' The paper thereafter imposes the substantially narrower standing assumption that Lambda is a finite-dimensional algebra over a field, and Proposition 3.9 is stated only for Lambda-mod under that assumption. No reduction from arbitrary artinian rings to finite-dimensional algebras over fields is given. Therefore the advertised generality is not established by the paper.
